source_refs.note: 4. Substrate Concentration: a main subheading of 5.4 Factors affecting the rate of enzyme action, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 136-136.

blocks.text: If there are enzyme molecules with vacant active sites, an increase in substrate concentration will increase the rate of reaction. If enzyme concentration is kept constant and the amount of substrate is increased, a point is reached where any further increase in substrate does not increase the rate of reaction any more.

When enzyme molecules are free (at low substrate concentration) new substrate molecules bind with the available active sites and so more products are formed in the given time i.e., rate of enzyme action is increased. But when all active sites of enzymes are occupied (at high substrate concentration), any more substrate molecules do not find free active sites and so reaction rate does not increase (Fig.5.8)

blocks.alt: A graph of rate of reaction against substrate concentration. The line rises straight from the origin, then bends and runs flat along a dotted level; an arrow at the bend is labelled No more active sites for substrate.
blocks.caption: Figure 5.8: Effect of substrate concentration on enzyme activity (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 5.8).
